new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (61,573 bytes; full paper text extracted from the Wayback copy of academia.edu/7152884, whose HTML title is "(PDF) A preliminary phonology of Ngochang | Douglas Inglis - Academia.edu"). All quoted sentences are present verbatim and the page attributions hold against the running headers "Ngochang Phonology Doug and Connie Inglis N" (header 7 at byte 16546, 8 at 19427, 9 at 21988, 10 at 24207): fn. 6 "The phonological feature of stress is not part of this preliminary study but would be important for helping to establish a phonological level breath group (see also Wannemacher 1998:66 for Zaiwa)" at byte 18673 = p. 7; "The Ngochang syllables are of the following types, CV, CVC, CVVC, CVC…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ngochang/Achang is a tone language (three contrastive tones in unchecked syllables, two registers in checked ones). The only stress statement is structural: every full syllable (CV, CVC, CVVC, CVCC) is a stressed, tone-bearing syllable, while a reduced presyllable V (often schwa) is unstressed and cannot be the sole stressed syllable of a word; i.e. sesquisyllabic words are weak-strong (minor syllable + stressed major syllable). The authors explicitly exclude word/phrase stress from the study, so no rule for stress placement in polysyllabic words is given. Dai & Cui 1985 (Husa/Longchuan dialect proper) say the same thing in Chinese terms without using the word stress: some disyllables have a weakened (弱化) first syllable whose a becomes [ə], 'slightly lighter and shorter' (p. 2, p. 22).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the study is preliminary and based on a 430-item wordlist. Dai & Cui 1985 p. 22 add that weakening also affects some a-nucleus diphthongs and closed rhymes, and that ŋa 'fish' and no 'cow' weaken to kă- in compounds.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonology of citation forms (wordlist elicitation); the breath group / phrase level is explicitly left for future work.
new_statements.identity_note: Inglis & Inglis 2003 (the quoted source) describe Ngochang as spoken around Myitkyina, Kachin State, Myanmar; Glottolog treats Ngochang as an alternative name of acha1249 (ISO acn, countries CN;MM) and Inglis notes the Ngochang and the Chinese Achang say it is the same language, while their phoneme inventory is 'comparable to the phonology of Achang in China (Dai and Cui 1985)'. The acha1249 reference lect proper, Husa (户撒) in Longchuan County, is described by Dai & Cui 1985, which is silent on stress but reports the same unstressed/weakened presyllable pattern (p. 2, p. 22). Xiandao (Yingjiang County) is a separate Achangic variety also listed under acha1249's names; not covered here.

sources.locator: §2.1.2 'Ambiguous segments' p. 8 and §2.1.2/2.2 p. 9; footnote 6 on p. 7 (page numbers from the running header 'Ngochang Phonology Doug and Connie Inglis N' in the extracted text)
sources.note: Full syllables (CV, CVC, CVVC, CVCC) are stressed; a presyllable V (often reduced to schwa) is unstressed; tone is obligatory in stressed syllables; there are no stressed *V(C) syllables (pp. 8-9). Footnote 6 (p. 7): the phonological feature of stress is not part of this preliminary study but would matter for establishing the breath group. Three contrastive tones (54, 3, 31) in unchecked syllables; tense/modal voice quality. Read from the full paper text embedded in the Wayback copy of the academia.edu page; the PDF itself is login-walled.

sources.citation: 戴庆厦、崔志超 (Dai Qingxia & Cui Zhichao). 1985. 阿昌语简志 [Achangyu jianzhi, A sketch of the Achang language]. 中国少数民族语言简志丛书. 北京: 民族出版社. 135+ pp. Reference dialect: Husa, Longchuan County (陇川县户撒).
sources.note: No stress (重音) section. Four tones: 高平 55, 低降 31, 高升 35, 全降 51 (p. 16); ten syllable types (p. 17); rich sandhi: tone sandhi, epenthesis, weakening, syllable fusion, syllable loss (pp. 17-23). Weakening: '(四) 有弱化音节，出现在一部分双音节词的前一音节上' (p. 2) and '在双音节词里，前一音节的韵母如果是 a，多出现弱化现象。弱化后的 a 读[ə]，音值略轻且短' (p. 22) -- i.e. reduced, lighter and shorter first syllables in some disyllables; nothing on where word stress falls.
